intro: Thailand's Michelin-listed seafood is the stuff locals actually queue for. Start with Here Hai and its legendary crab fried rice, piled so high with lump crab meat that the whole scene rushed to copy it, then Chai in Nonthaburi for a whole crispy-skinned grouper fried in fish sauce at just 390 baht, and Kin Kub Koi for its steamed egg crab in fresh milk. Every one is a Bib Gourmand, so you eat well without sweating the bill.
quickAnswerHtml: A roundup of 8 seafood restaurants from the Michelin Guide Thailand, all Bib Gourmand, led by Here Hai and its famous overflowing crab fried rice in Bangkok.

blocks.html: Thailand's Michelin-listed seafood is the stuff locals actually queue for. Start with Here Hai and its legendary crab fried rice, piled so high with lump crab meat that the whole scene rushed to copy it, then Chai in Nonthaburi for a whole crispy-skinned grouper fried in fish sauce at just 390 baht, and Kin Kub Koi for its steamed egg crab in fresh milk. Every one is a Bib Gourmand, so you eat well without sweating the bill.

blocks.name: Ann Tha Din Daeng
blocks.descHtml:
Budget around THB 300–800 per person (Wongnai places it in the THB 501–1,000 band). Small dishes start from around THB 100, while the flagship fried river prawn with salt runs THB 450 per prawn. Important: cash only, so bring enough. There's no online booking system of any kind — just walk in, or call ahead at +66 81 695 0597 (easier if you can speak Thai). The restaurant is open Wednesday–Sunday 11:00–20:00 (Google lists 10:30 as opening time), closed Monday–Tuesday.

Getting there is easier than you'd think — take the Gold Line to Khlong San station, then walk about 5 more minutes to the restaurant on Tha Din Daeng Road, in the Khlong San area on the Thonburi side. The best time to go is right at opening or an early lunch, since the seafood supply is limited per day, popular dishes sell out fast, and several reviewers have found the restaurant closed early once stock runs out. Tables turn over quickly thanks to heavy takeaway demand, so the wait shouldn't be long outside peak hours. If you're set on the river prawn specifically, calling ahead before you leave your hotel is the surest bet. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Khlong San / Tha Din Daeng (Thonburi 'Little China Town')
mustOrder: Clams with sweet chilli paste and Thai basil
Crab meat in yellow chilli curry
blocks.bestFor: Seafood lovers who want Bib Gourmand-level fried river prawn with salt at down-to-earth prices, and who enjoy exploring the old Thonburi side

blocks.name: Chai
blocks.descHtml:
Budget per head around THB 250–500 is light for a Bib Gourmand-level restaurant — crab fried rice starts at THB 75, squid in fish sauce THB 230, fried grouper with fish sauce THB 390, and the large curry-powder sea crab THB 800. The restaurant takes cash only, so bring enough. Most tables are walk-in, but if you're coming as a larger group you can call ahead at 063-998-3986 or 088-978-1558 — no deposit needed, and no online queue system to fight over.

The restaurant is open 15:00–01:00 (Sundays until around midnight) and closed on the second and fourth Tuesday of every month. Early evening is busiest, so if you'd rather skip the wait, go in the late afternoon or after 9pm. Getting there means driving or taking a taxi to Soi Samakkhi 38, Tha Sai, Mueang Nonthaburi, since the MRT Pink Line's Samakkhi station is over 2 km away — too far to walk. On the plus side, the restaurant has its own car park and an air-con zone to sit in. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Soi Samakkhi 38, Tha Sai, Mueang Nonthaburi
blocks.signature: Fried grouper with fish sauce — crisp skin, tender flesh, whole fish for THB 390
blocks.bestFor: A late-night meal with friends or family who want serious seafood at khao tom prices — best for people with a car, since the location isn't within walking distance of any train station
blocks.zone: Soi Samakkhi 38, Tha Sai, Mueang Nonthaburi

blocks.name: Here Hai
blocks.descHtml:
Budget around THB 251-500 per person. The signature dish, Khao Phat Khote Poo, runs about 480-510 baht, Khote Kang Kratiam Prik Thai is 565 baht, and Khote Hoi Chelly Kaphrao is 385 baht. The restaurant doesn't take table bookings through any channel — there's no online system, and the only way in is to queue at the door, which runs long nearly every day. The trick is to arrive before opening at 10:00 to grab a table in the first round, or aim for the 16:00 afternoon slot, which is noticeably quieter than lunchtime — just be aware that the afternoon slot is very short, since the restaurant closes at 17:30. Call 063-219-9100 with any questions.

Getting there: the restaurant sits in the middle of Ekkamai Road between Soi 10-12, about 1.5 km from BTS Ekkamai. It's walkable but takes around 20 minutes — a motorcycle taxi from the mouth of the soi is much faster. If you're driving, note that there's no parking at the restaurant; park at Don Don Donki mall nearby and walk over instead. Open Tuesday-Sunday 10:00-15:00 and 16:00-17:30, closed Mondays. If you'd rather skip the queue entirely, the restaurant also delivers through LINE MAN. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Khao Phat Khote Poo — fried rice piled with a mountain of crab meat, the dish that made the whole industry follow suit
mustOrder: Kaeng Khote Poo Bai Cha Phlu
blocks.bestFor: Seafood fans ready to queue at lunchtime for a plate piled with the original crab fried rice

blocks.name: Kin Kub Koi
blocks.descHtml:
Per-person budget is flexible — starting around THB 250 for something light like fried prawn cakes, and running to THB 1,000+ if you go for the steamed egg crab with fresh milk (~THB 720) plus river prawns priced by weight. Important: the restaurant takes cash and bank transfer only, no credit cards, and does not accept table bookings under any circumstance — walk-in only. Call 094-666-9289 with any questions.

The restaurant sits on Phutthamonthon Sai 2 Road in the Thawi Watthana area, western Thonburi — no train line reaches it, so driving is the best option, since the parking lot is genuinely spacious. Open daily 10:30–20:30, with seating available until around 21:30. Weekday afternoons are fairly relaxed, but weekends draw big crowds — get there before the 10:30 opening or avoid the lunch rush. The restaurant has four seating zones and turns tables over quickly, so the wait is shorter than it looks. One more rule to know: no outside food allowed in. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Steamed egg crab with fresh milk
blocks.priceRange: Around THB 250–1,000+ per person, depending on order
mustOrder: Steamed egg crab with fresh milk
blocks.bestFor: A family seafood outing for weekend crowds who want steamed egg crab and river prawns at wholesale-fresh prices, and anyone with a car who wants to eat well without heading into the city

blocks.name: Krachang Khao Lak
blocks.descHtml:
Krachang Khao Lak sits at Thap Lamu Pier in the Lam Kaen zone, southern Khao Lak, right by the pier that departs for the Similan Islands — a short drive south from the Khao Lak beach strip. Open 12:00–21:00 (some sources like Wongnai list closing at 20:00, so it's worth giving yourself extra time) and closed every Tuesday — do not plan a Tuesday visit. Budget runs around 250–500 THB per head; if you order fresh seafood sold by weight, the price moves up with the size of the fish.

The restaurant is mostly walk-in, but the restaurant's page says advance table bookings are accepted — call 095-656-0862 or message the "Krachang Khao Lak" Facebook page. The best time to go is late afternoon into evening, when the view over Thap Lamu Bay and the mangrove forest looks best in the softer light, and it's also exactly when divers coming off Similan boats tend to stop by. If you've booked a Similan trip, it's worth planning dinner here afterward — you can walk straight from the boat to the restaurant with no need to drive further. Dress is casual; it's an open-air waterfront raft-style restaurant. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Thai-style sashimi from the restaurant's own fish pens
mustOrder: Thai-style raw fish sashimi / fresh grouper salad
Fish shabu, broth simmered from fish bones for 8 hours
Sour curry with fish head and coconut shoots
blocks.bestFor: Fresh seafood lovers from the fish pens, Thai-style raw fish by the bay, and divers back from a Similan trip who want a beautiful end to the day on the water

blocks.name: Lucky Seafood
blocks.descHtml:
Budget per head runs around THB 250–600 depending on how much seafood you order (Wongnai places it in the THB 251–500 band, while diners who go all-in on a seafood dinner often land at THB 500–600). Important: the shop takes cash only, so bring enough. The only way to book is by calling +66 94 965 1881 — there's no online booking system, and calling ahead is near-essential in almost every case, since the shop has only around 4–7 tables. Regulars tend to pre-order their dishes right when they book, since the tiny family kitchen cooks one plate at a time — doing so cuts down the wait a lot.

The restaurant sits on Phran Nok–Phutthamonthon Sai 4 Road in the Bang Phrom area of Taling Chan, with no train station within walking distance (MRT Fai Chai is about 1.5 km away) — the easiest way there is to drive and park roadside out front, or call a taxi/ride service. It's open evenings only, Wednesday–Sunday, 16:00–22:00, closed Monday–Tuesday. If you haven't booked, arrive right at the 4pm opening for the best chance at a table. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Stir-fried crab meat with bird's eye chilli
mustOrder: Stir-fried crab meat with bird's eye chilli
blocks.bestFor: A fresh, family-cooked seafood dinner at wallet-friendly prices for people chasing Bib Gourmand spots on the Thonburi side

blocks.name: Pa Ting (Don Sak)
blocks.descHtml:
A very comfortable budget for a MICHELIN-listed restaurant, running around 250–500 THB per person, and it takes credit cards too. It's walk-in, no reservation needed, but if you want to check ahead or you're coming as a large group, you can call 063-982-6959 (the number listed in the MICHELIN Guide) or 077-371-126 and 092-956-5593. Hours are Monday 9:00–20:30 and Tuesday–Sunday 9:30–20:30, with the restaurant's Facebook page noting last order at 20:30. Dress is casual.

The restaurant sits by the water at Pak Khlong Don Sak, Don Sak district, Surat Thani, around 10 minutes by car from the ferry pier to Koh Samui/Koh Pha Ngan. That's exactly the planning tip — if you're heading to Samui by car and ferry, build in time to stop for lunch or dinner right before boarding. Or if you're on your way back from the islands, it's perfectly placed for a stop before the long drive into town. The busiest times are around ferry departure and arrival slots, so if you want to sit back and enjoy the water without fighting for a table, aim to come a bit before or after those times. Dishes that should be on your table: crab and cha khram curry, salted grey mullet spicy salad, and boiled white clams with lemongrass. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Pak Khlong Don Sak, Don Sak district
mustOrder: Sour curry with fresh grey mullet
Stir-fried prawns with sataw beans and shrimp paste
blocks.bestFor: Stop for real Southern-style seafood before or after the ferry to Koh Samui-Pha Ngan — a light-budget family meal by the water

faq.q: Which Michelin seafood spot should I hit first
faq.a: Here Hai in Vadhana, Bangkok is the one to pin first. Its crab fried rice comes buried under big lumps of crab meat, the dish that set the trend everyone copied, which is exactly why the line runs long most days.

faq.q: Which one is the best value
faq.a: All eight are Bib Gourmand, Michelin's stamp for great food at a friendly price. Chai in Nonthaburi makes the case plainly, serving a whole grouper fried in fish sauce with crispy skin and juicy flesh for 390 baht.

faq.q: What crab dish is a must-try
faq.a: There are several ways to go crab: Here Hai's crab fried rice, the steamed egg crab in fresh milk at Kin Kub Koi, stir-fried crab meat with bird's eye chili at Lucky Seafood, and the crab curry with sea samphire at Pa Ting in Don Sak, Surat Thani.

faq.q: Where do I go for the freshest fish and prawns
faq.a: For fish straight from the source, try Krachang Khao Lak in Phang-Nga, which serves Thai fish sashimi from its own sea pen. For prawns, head to Ann Tha Din Daeng in Bangkok for salt-fried river prawns at 450 baht each.

faq.q: Which provinces are these seafood restaurants in
faq.a: Most sit in Bangkok, including Here Hai, Kin Kub Koi, Lucky Seafood and Ann Tha Din Daeng. The rest spread to Nonthaburi (Chai), Phang-Nga (Krachang Khao Lak) and Surat Thani (Pa Ting).
